persona.who: 22, wants to be a filmmaker, father is a government doctor who wants him to do MBBS or at least MBA. Fights every dinner.
persona.note: papa says films are for rich kids and I should do MBA. we fight every night. I love him and I also feel like he doesn't see me at all. mummy cries in the kitchen

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call being seen as less than you are, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being told who to be to standing in what you are, with the words to say so without losing the love.

week_beats.story: A daughter who questioned her father's vision and stood in her own shows you what it looks like to be seen by yourself first.

understanding.core_struggle: A young woman is being told by her father that her love of films is not real and that she should do an MBA instead, while her mother cries and she feels unseen.
understanding.mirror: What you told us: father dismisses her interest in films as rich kids' work.
understanding.insight: You are not asking for too much. You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Being seen as less than you are by the one who loves you most, and the loneliness of knowing he does not see the person you are becoming. I keep fighting with my parents.
queries.diagnose: When a parent sees only a role they chose for you, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A daughter of a learned house, dismissed by her father for choosing a path he did not expect, who stood in her truth and found her footing on her own terms.

weeks: The woman he does not see

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse.sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते । क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
verse.line: This smallness of heart isn't who you are. Shake it off and stand up.
verse.translation: Do not give in to this unmanliness, Partha; it does not become you. Throw off this petty weakness of heart and rise, scorcher of enemies.
verse.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.
verse.misuse: Not 'feelings are weakness' or 'man up'. It is a friend reminding you of your strength, said once, then explained for 700 verses.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.meaning: Krishna is looking at Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna has dropped his bow and is crying, saying he cannot fight his own family. Krishna tells him to stop this collapse. He calls it a smallness of heart, not who Arjuna truly is. He asks him to stand up and face the moment.
verse.for_you: You are sitting with your phone, feeling torn and unseen again. Your father has told you your love for films is not real. This smallness you feel is not who you are. Stand up to it. Your truth is already there.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verse.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.
verse.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.

prasang.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna, who has laid down his weapons and refused to fight. Krishna asks why Arjuna is shrinking from his own nature. He tells him that it is better to walk one's own path, even if the steps are clumsy or imperfect. To wear another person's life like a borrowed coat will only bring a constant, low-grade fear. The fear is not in the imperfect walking. It is in the wrong shoes.
verse.for_you: Your father wants you in an MBA suit. That suit is not your shape. Walk in your own film-soaked shoes, even if the steps are uneven. The fear is in the borrowed coat, not in your own stride.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verse.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
verse.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: King Janaka sits before the young sage Ashtavakra and asks how a person becomes truly free. Ashtavakra tells him that the whole universe is strung on him and that by nature he is pure awareness. He warns the king not to fall into the smallness of mind. The truth is that you are the awareness watching your life, not the roles and worries that pass through it.
verse.for_you: You are not your parents' expectations or their tears. You are the awareness watching this fight. Hold on to the fact that you are wider than this room. The smallness belongs to them, not to you.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt or settle for too little. She says to set his mind on what is truly good and stop being afraid. He must pull himself together. The idea is that past defeat does not define him. The future is uncertain, but those who do not try will certainly fail.
verse.for_you: You are not finished. Your father's words are a small picture, but you are wider than that. Let your mind rest on what you know is good about yourself, and let the fear fall away for a moment.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verse.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verse.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verse.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.meaning: Ram speaks to Lakshman after hearing Hanuman for the first time. Hanuman, a stranger, had just spoken to them. His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained. They came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone. The verse proposes that fear jumps ahead of facts. Calm, clear words build trust fast.
verse.for_you: When you speak to your parents tonight, let your words be clear and even. You do not need to shout to be seen. A steady voice carries the truth better than a loud one.

verse.speaker: Brihaspati (retold by Bhishma)
verse.setting: Brihaspati counsels Indra on how to hold authority among difficult people.
verse.sanskrit: मृदुमप्यवमन्यन्ते तीक्ष्णादुद्विजते जनः / मातीक्ष्णो मा मृदुर्भूस्त्वं तीक्ष्णो भव मृदुर्भव
verse.line: People walk over the soft and fear the harsh. Be firm when it's needed, gentle when it's needed.
verse.translation: People look down even on the gentle, and they shrink from the harsh. Do not be only harsh, do not be only soft: be firm when firmness is needed and gentle when gentleness is.
verse.misuse: Firmness here means clarity, not cruelty.
verse.meaning: Brihaspati speaks to Indra about holding authority over difficult people. He tells him that people walk over the gentle and shrink from the harsh. The advice is to not be only harsh or only soft. Be firm when firmness is needed, and gentle when gentleness is needed.
verse.for_you: Your parents are not seeing the whole picture of who you are. You can speak with the same clarity as Brihaspati. You do not need to be harsh, but you do need to be firm. Tell them exactly what you are studying and why it matters to you. Let them see your truth.

story.title: Satyakama Jabala, the honest boy
story.story_hook: Satyakama wanted to study, but first he had to ask his mother a question she could not answer.
story.summary: A boy who wants to study asks his mother about his father's lineage. She tells him frankly she does not know, and he repeats this word for word to the teacher. The teacher accepts him for his honesty, sends him off with 400 weak cows, and the boy returns years later with a thousand, having learned from nature along the way, yet still asks his teacher to teach him.
story.lesson: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.

anchor.speaker: Jabala
anchor.setting: A boy asks his mother his lineage before seeking a teacher.
anchor.sanskrit: सा हैनमुवाच नाहमेतद्वेद तात यद्गोत्रस्त्वमसि बह्वहं चरन्ती परिचारिणी यौवने त्वामलभे साहमेतन्न वेद यद्गोत्रस्त्वमसि जबाला तु नामाहमस्मि सत्यकामो नाम त्वमसि स सत्यकाम एव जाबालो ब्रवीथा इति ॥
anchor.line: His mother said, 'I don't know your father's line. I am Jabala, you are Satyakama. Say exactly that.'
anchor.translation: She said to him: 'I do not know your lineage, my child. In my youth I moved about a great deal as a serving woman, and then I had you. So I do not know your lineage. My name is Jabala and your name is Satyakama. Just say you are Satyakama Jabala.'
anchor.why: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.

script: You are on your phone again, and the night feels torn again. Your father is telling you that your love for films is not real. Your mother is crying in the other room. You feel completely unseen. This is a heavy weight to carry alone.

Krishna looks at Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna has dropped his bow and is crying, saying he cannot fight his own family. Krishna tells him to stop this collapse. He calls it a smallness of heart, not who Arjuna truly is. He asks him to stand up and face the moment. And Krishna replied:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते, क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप.
In plain words: This smallness of heart isn't who you are. Shake it off and stand up.

Krishna is not saying your feelings are wrong. He is saying this collapse is not who you are. Admitting you are confused and asking for help is where clarity begins. You are not weak for feeling torn. You are human. But this smallness is a choice to shrink. You can stand up to it.
Right now, in your room, you can stand up. Let your parents have their words. But you hold your truth. Your love for films is real. You do not have to shrink to fit their picture.
You are already whole. What is the first thing you will do?

depth.points: This smallness of heart is not who they are. It is a temporary cloud, not the sky. Their truth is already there, waiting for them to stand up to it.
depth.practice: Write down one line about what they love about films, just for them.
depth.question: What would it feel like to stand in what they are?
